sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Identify the money market instruments: (a) Issued by the RBI at a discount and redeemed at face value. (b) Issued by highly reputed companies as an unsecured promissory note.
questions.answer: (a) Treasury bill. (b) Commercial paper.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The primary market is also called the ______ market. (b) The secondary market is also called the ______.
questions.answer: (a) new issue. (b) stock exchange (stock market).

questions.q: State true or false: (i) Money market deals in cash. (ii) Listing is mandatory in the secondary market.
questions.answer: (i) False – it deals in short-term credit instruments. (ii) True.

questions.q: Name the three functions of financial markets.
questions.answer: Price discovery, providing liquidity and reducing transaction costs.

questions.q: A treasury bill was bought for Rs 9,200 and redeemed after a year for Rs 10,000. Find the yield.
Expand: (i) IPO (ii) FPO (iii) SEBI.
questions.answer: (i) Initial Public Offering. (ii) Follow-on Public Offering. (iii) Securities and Exchange Board of India.

questions.q: Rashmi bought 200 shares at Rs 210 and sold them at Rs 235 without taking delivery. Find the amount she receives (before brokerage).
questions.answer:
Difference per share = 235 − 210 = Rs 25.
Amount = 200 × 25 = Rs 5,000.

questions.q: Name the instrument used by banks to meet temporary cash needs for one day to a fortnight.
questions.answer: Call money.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Give the meaning of 'Price Discovery' as an important function of financial markets.
questions.answer: The interaction of buyers and sellers in the financial market determines the price of a financial instrument and helps allocate funds among those who need them.

questions.q: Identify and give the meaning of the money market instrument whose interest rate is called 'Call Rate'.
questions.answer: Call money: money borrowed and lent by banks for a day to a fortnight, repayable on demand, to meet temporary cash needs.

questions.q: Define financial market.
questions.answer: A transmission mechanism between investors (lenders) and borrowers through which the transfer of funds is facilitated.

questions.q: What is a stock exchange?
questions.answer: An organised market where existing approved securities such as shares, debentures and bonds are bought and sold regularly by its members.

questions.q: What is meant by rolling settlement?
questions.answer: Transactions are settled after a fixed number of days from the trade date (e.g. T+2), by electronic transfer through demat accounts.

questions.q: State any two limitations of stock exchanges.
questions.answer: Excessive speculation causes wide price fluctuations; prices are affected by unpredictable political, social and economic factors.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the advantages of stock exchanges to society.
questions.answer: It induces savings and investment and so aids capital formation; supports the new issue market and industrial growth; moves resources to profitable units; reflects economic health; and facilitates government borrowing.

questions.q: Explain any three functions of a stock exchange.
questions.answer: It gives a ready market for securities, provides information on prices and ensures safety in dealings (also mobilises savings and acts as a barometer).

questions.q: Explain any three money market instruments.
questions.answer: Treasury bill (RBI, up to 364 days), commercial paper (reputed companies, 15 days to one year) and certificate of deposit (banks, 91 days to one year).

questions.q: Explain the functions of financial markets.
questions.answer: Price discovery, liquidity for financial instruments and lower transaction costs through an organised platform.

questions.q: Distinguish between investment and speculation transactions.
questions.answer: Investment: delivery and full payment for income and long-term gain; speculation: buying or selling to gain from price differences, settled by paying or receiving the difference.

questions.q: State the advantages of stock exchanges to investors.
questions.answer: Ready facility to buy and sell, safety of dealings, regular price information and loans from banks against securities.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: What is meant by 'Capital Market'? Give any four points of distinction between 'Primary Market' and 'Secondary Market'.
questions.answer: The capital market deals in medium- and long-term funds. Primary versus secondary: function (raising funds by fresh issue versus ready market for existing securities); participants (institutions, mutual funds, underwriters, investors versus these plus stockbrokers); listing (not required versus mandatory); price (set by management with SEBI norms versus demand and supply).

questions.q: Distinguish between capital market and money market.
questions.answer: Period (long versus short); securities (shares and debentures versus bills and commercial paper); participants (stockbrokers, mutual funds versus banks); regulator (SEBI versus RBI).

questions.q: Explain the functions of a stock exchange.
questions.answer: Ready market, price information, safety in dealings, mobilisation of savings and capital formation, barometer of the economy and efficient allocation of funds.

questions.q: Explain the money market instruments with their maturity periods.
questions.answer: Call money (1 day to a fortnight), treasury bills (up to 364 days), commercial paper (15 days to one year), certificates of deposit (91 days to one year) and trade bills (within one year).
